title: Move Zeroes In Place
hints: Use two indices: one reading every element, one marking where the next non-zero goes.
Whenever the reader finds a non-zero, swap it into the write position and advance the writer.
`var write = 0; for read in nums.indices where nums[read] != 0 { nums.swapAt(write, read); write += 1 }`.
jsBridge: In JS the array is passed by reference, so a function mutates it directly. In Swift the array is a value, and in-place mutation requires `inout` (with `&` at the call site). Otherwise the function gets a copy.

compass.q: In JS any function you pass an array to can mutate it. How does `inout` make mutation visible at the call site, and why do Swift APIs prefer returning new arrays?
In-place with two pointers vs `filter { $0 != 0 } + zeros`: which allocates? Does allocation matter here?
Look at the standard library's `partition(by:)`. Is it stable? Why can't it replace this solution?
When does in-place mutation of large arrays matter on iOS: image pixels, audio buffers? What does `withUnsafeMutableBufferPointer` give you?
